originality.rationale: The inspected 2017 source defines the same map and gaps, proves almost-everywhere entrance, and gives an unweighted Lebesgue survivor matrix. It does not determine the dimension of the nonentrance set; this requires constructing disjoint inverse first-return similarities with all pressure exponents and deriving the critical dimension laws. It likewise does not state the full compound-geometric first-entrance distribution with independent entry-location law. Targeted web and semantic searches found related escape and dimension work on distinct systems, not covering the present exact family. Generic Moran/renewal techniques are credited. Residual equivalence risk in older symbolic dynamics literature remains.
residual_risks: Generic graph-directed IFS, kneading or open-dynamical-systems literature may already specialize a dimension equation to equivalent cyclic-gap maps under other notation.

value.rationale: The motivating 2017 theorem establishes Li–Yorke chaos together with almost-everywhere eventual period p, but leaves the geometry and quantitative capture of its Lebesgue-null exceptional set unspecified. The exact Hausdorff dimension, full dimension range 0 to 1 despite zero Lebesgue measure, and sharp dimension-edge laws identify a natural invariant that matters for distinguishing dynamically noncaptured states. The simultaneous exact first-entry distribution, phase selection, and critical divergence quantify the physical-time persistence that the qualitative theorem cannot measure. This is a natural all-parameter calculation rather than an arbitrary finite parameter slice or a small numerical improvement.
